references.source:
Amy Kim and Seung Kim\.
Bishnupriya \(manipuri\) speakers in bangladesh: a sociolinguistic survey\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008\-003, SIL International, 2008\.
Site codes are a Tilakpur, b Soi Sri, c Gulerhaor, d Dhonitila, e Machimpur, f Madhapur and 0 standard Bangla\. Gulerhaor, Dhonitila, Soi Sri and Machimpur are Rajar Gang villages; Tilakpur and Madhapur are Madoi Gang villages\. One item 267 control code is visibly printed as lowercase o and is interpreted as 0 in the audit\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/resources/archives/9100](https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/9100)\.
references.progress: Appendix B.3, "Wordlists": every printed response for the 307-item list, expanded across the six Bishnupriya village codes. The standard Bangla code 0, nine prompt headings with no responses, lexical-similarity calculations and all non-lexical appendices are audit-only
references.provenance: Freely published SIL Electronic Survey Report. The official SIL archive record and browser-rendered PDF are the bibliographic authority. Because the command-line publisher endpoint returned a Cloudflare HTML challenge, extraction used the fixed-layout text transcript and 2048-pixel page rasters in public Slideshare copy 2624796 as a mechanical scaffold. Reproducible extraction and the complete page and glyph fingerprints are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_bishnupriya_2008; per-record audit data are in data/other/forms/raw_data/20260828-sil-bishnupriya-audit.csv; installed rows are in data/other/forms/20260828-sil-bishnupriya.csv
